{"summary":"Read-only audit completed. Inventory verified against `bin/msw:main` (lines 1819-1904), `show_help` (1765-1817), installer options (setup.sh:10-31), all requested documentation, and test cases; no project-wide tests, linters, or formatters were run.

Classification for the current native-app surface:
SAFE APP ACTIONS: `zed WORKSPACE [PATH]`, `open WORKSPACE [PORT] [SCHEME]`, `url`, `ports`, `start`, `status`/`ps`, `disk`, `clone`, `repos`, quick `check`, supervised `tunnel`, `github status` (including bare `github`), `docs` (including `commands`/`test-report` aliases), `version`/`--version`/`-V`, and `help`/`--help`/`-h`. Note that `open`, `zed`, `disk`, and several repository actions automatically start stopped VMs through `ensure_running` (bin/msw:356-379).
APP ACTIONS REQUIRING CONFIRMATION: `pull` (changes a checkout), `push` including `--yes`/`-y` and `--force-with-lease`, `stop`, `restart`, `resize`, `clean` and especially `clean --volumes`, `upgrade`, `update`, `check --deep`, `backup` (temporarily stops running VMs), `restore` including `--yes`/`-y`, `github verify` (creates/pushes/deletes a remote branch), and `github remove`. Existing confirmations cover only push (`push_impl`, bin/msw:984-1086, prompt at 1033-1036) and restore (`cmd_restore`, 1650-1749, prompt at 1709-1719); the other destructive/disruptive commands currently run immediately.
APP-ONLY SETUP/SETTINGS ACTIONS: `identity`, `github setup ... [--read-only]`, `host repair`, and `./setup.sh` with no option or `--rebuild-base`, `--recreate-workspaces`, `--reset-config`, or `--help`. `host repair` performs sudo/LaunchDaemon, `/etc/hosts`, loopback, SSH-key, and SSH-config mutations (bin/msw:655-741); setup installs Homebrew/tools, writes shell startup files, installs MSW, creates/recreates VMs, and runs a deep check (setup.sh:38-98,130-160,251-317). These belong in onboarding or Settings, with macOS authorization UI and explicit impact summaries.
TERMINAL/UNSUPPORTED AS CURRENTLY IMPLEMENTED: `dev`, `playgrounds`, `personal`, and generic `shell` require an SSH TTY (`cmd_shell`, bin/msw:474-482); `exec` is arbitrary guest command execution (582-587); `metrics` hardcodes an in-place `--watch` process (569-574); and unrestricted `logs WORKSPACE [MSB OPTIONS]` is a passthrough stream (576-580). The app should open an external terminal for shells, omit arbitrary exec from its public UI, and use dedicated structured metrics/log APIs. The internal `__github-verify-transaction` command (1890-1895) is not user-facing.

Machine-interface findings: there is no global JSON mode, schema version, structured error, progress channel, or stable exit-code taxonomy. Human ANSI output is produced by `note`/`warn`/`ok` (bin/msw:33-36); `status`, `ports`, `disk`, `github status`, backup paths, push plans, checks, and child Git/MSB output are formatted for humans (511-595,1015-1031,1321-1329,1390-1477,1503-1582). The one internal JSON call, `msb status ... --format json`, is reduced with whitespace removal and substring matching rather than decoded JSON (`sandbox_running`, 249-257). Tests likewise capture pipes rather than TTYs (`run_cmd`, tests/test_suite.py:40-65) and assert human fragments or split human lines, including URL output (415-429), GitHub status (518-534,644-665), push cancellation (1010-1024), and backup archive discovery (1112-1117). The fake MSB only minimally models JSON status and returns empty metrics/logs (tests/fake_msb.py:531-544), so JSON schemas, ANSI-free output, structured failures, backpressure, TTY refusal, and cancellation semantics are untested.

Proposed minimal stable contract: add an `msw app` namespace while leaving the human CLI unchanged. Provide `msw app handshake --format json`, `state [--workspace W]`, `repositories --workspace W`, `github-state [--workspace W]`, `plan ACTION ...`, `apply PLAN_ID --confirmation TOKEN`, `metrics --workspace W --format jsonl`, `logs --workspace W --format jsonl`, and `tunnel --workspace W --remote-port P [--local-port P] --format jsonl`. Every finite command should emit exactly one UTF-8 JSON object on stdout: `{schemaVersion:'1.0',requestId,ok,command,result,warnings,error}`; errors should contain stable `code`, `message`, `details`, and `recovery`, never credentials. Progress and long-lived events should be JSON Lines on an explicit inherited event FD, not mixed with the final stdout object. Standardize exits as 0 success, 64 usage, 69 dependency/unavailable, 73 conflict/lock, 77 authorization, 78 configuration/migration, 130 cancelled, and 1 operation failure. `plan` must return normalized arguments, effects, preconditions, expiry, and an opaque confirmation token bound to that exact plan; `apply` must reject stale state. This replaces blind app use of `--yes`.

The app should launch executable URLs directly with argument arrays—never through a login shell—and resolve the helper first at `~/.local/bin/msw`, then a bundled helper used for onboarding. Finder-launched apps cannot assume shell PATH. Setup currently prepends `~/.local/bin` only in `.zprofile`/`.zshrc` (setup.sh:43-46), installs MSW there (81-85), and both scripts discover dependencies mainly through `command -v` (`bin/msw:20-31`, setup.sh:62-73). `handshake` should therefore run even when config is missing and return absolute resolved paths/capabilities for MSW, MSB, SSH, Git, curl, jq, zstd, tar, and helpers. It should search explicit macOS locations and accept validated absolute overrides. The current sourced `config.sh` is executable shell (`bin/msw:4-10`), so the app must not parse it; expose normalized configuration in handshake JSON and eventually migrate app-owned state to a versioned data file. Use `Process` pipes, `NO_COLOR=1`, explicit HOME and PATH, process groups, SIGTERM followed by bounded SIGKILL, and cancellation-aware cleanup. Do not allocate a PTY except when handing a shell to a terminal. Existing internal guest operations correctly use `msb exec --no-tty` (381-397); docs already avoid a pager on non-TTY stdout (`cmd_docs`, 1751-1763). For current MSB capabilities, use its structured status/inspect/metrics output and JSONL logs behind the MSW adapter; the app should not depend directly on unpinned MSB schemas.

GitHub App migration requirements: the repository currently assumes two long-lived fine-grained PATs per workspace (`docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md:3-16,31-114`), stored under Keychain services `msw.github.read` and `msw.github.write` with workspace accounts (`bin/msw:12-15,89-152`) plus flat metadata files (`metadata_*`, 154-176). The guest token is bound through `GH_TOKEN@github.com,api.github.com` (`config.sh:50-52`; `bind_github_read_token`, bin/msw:867-884; setup.sh:282-284), while host Git askpass reads the write PAT from Keychain. The current working-tree regression demonstrates that a source `GH_TOKEN` must be present for every MSB operation that reads the secret-bearing sandbox configuration (`cmd_github_verify`, bin/msw:1135-1139; tests/test_suite.py:536-545; tests/fake_msb.py:249-254).

A native app must not embed a GitHub App private key or pass tokens in argv/environment. Use an authenticated broker/XPC helper: persist only installation identity and a renewable app session in Keychain, mint short-lived installation tokens on demand, request a repository- and permission-narrowed `contents:read` token for guest traffic and a separate `contents:write` token for explicit host pushes, and pass only a credential-handle or inherited FD to MSW. Replace both the SSH proxy’s static read-token lookup and host Git askpass’s static write-token lookup with that helper. Schema-v2 metadata should record provider, installation ID/account/owner, repository selection, access mode, verification repository, expiry/refresh state, and migration status; secrets remain excluded from backups, preserving the existing boundary documented at `docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md:240-247` and implemented at bin/msw:1480-1491,1560-1568.

Migration must detect legacy Keychain presence without exposing values and report `provider:'legacy-pat'` plus `migrationRequired:true`. Perform an atomic sequence under the existing per-workspace lock (`github_lock_acquire`, bin/msw:220-240): authorize/install the GitHub App; mint and validate the read token; prove guest push rejection; validate the host-only push and cleanup path; switch metadata and secret binding; then delete legacy PAT items. Retain the old PAT configuration as rollback state until verification succeeds, mirroring `cmd_github_setup` transaction/rollback behavior (1204-1318) and its interruption/quarantine tests (tests/test_suite.py:564-643,712-902). Keep one GitHub owner/installation per workspace initially because the current single `GH_TOKEN` binding cannot route among multiple installations; multi-owner support requires a repository-aware credential proxy. Add contract tests for JSON schemas/errors, legacy detection and atomic migration, token refresh/expiry during start/SSH/push, broker outage, permission narrowing, cancellation, and proof that no token reaches output, argv, environment snapshots, state files, or backups.

Verification: all requested files and the complete command dispatcher/test inventory were inspected; command aliases and installer modes were cross-checked against help and documentation. No files were edited. The worktree already contained unrelated modifications and untracked files before the audit; they were left untouched.","filesChanged":[]}
